title: Service Visit Record and Vehicle Holds under Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
**Service-to-sales bulletin.** A buyer who services a vehicle with the group is held longer. On a hold extension of a reserved deal under the Vehicle Purchase Agreements, service-visit days are added to the extension length. The count is read from the buyer's service account in **Service Accounts and Repair Orders**: repair orders with a customer-pay concern line A, that is, a customer-pay labor charge on line A, closed in the window.

**Rule.**
- At least **4** such repair orders in the last 12 whole months before the handling date: **2 days** are added.
- At least **2** but fewer than **4**: **1 day** is added.
- Otherwise no service-visit days are added.

**Window.** A service repair order falls in the last 12 whole months when fewer than 12 whole calendar months have passed from its line date to the handling date. The line date is the date line A was closed. A month is whole once the same day of the month is reached.

| Repair orders with a customer-pay line A closed in the window | Service-visit days added |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | None |
| 2 or 3 | 1 |
| 4 or more | 2 |

**What does not count.**
- A repair order whose line A was not on customer pay.
- A repair order with customer-pay work only on later concern lines.
- A repair order closed 12 or more whole months before the handling date.

**Hypothetical illustration.** Over the past year a buyer's service account shows three repair orders with customer-pay line A labor, and two more with only warranty work on line A. Three qualifying repair orders gives 1 day.
